evals.name: observed-failure-builds-loop-first
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug checkout times out for orders over $1,000 but works fine for small orders.
evals.expected_output: Starts at Phase 1 by constructing a fast, deterministic, agent-runnable pass/fail reproduction loop before hypothesizing, and does not jump straight to guessing the cause.
expectations: Begins with Phase 1 — constructing a fast, deterministic, agent-runnable reproduction signal (failing test, curl/HTTP script, harness, etc.)
Does NOT skip to proposing a fix or root cause before a reproduction loop exists
Treats the tight loop as the load-bearing artifact and gates Phase 2 on having a loop it believes in

evals.name: no-loop-possible-is-the-deliverable
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug users report the app 'sometimes feels laggy' — I have no way to reproduce it, no logs, no access to their environment, and no capture.
evals.expected_output: When a loop genuinely cannot be built, it stops and says so explicitly, lists what was tried, and asks for environment access or a captured artifact — rather than proceeding to hypothesize without a loop.
expectations: Explicitly reports that a reproduction loop cannot be built with the given information
Lists the loop-construction strategies attempted and asks for environment access, a captured artifact (HAR/log/recording), or instrumentation permission
Does NOT proceed to Phase 3 hypothesizing without a loop

evals.name: multiple-falsifiable-hypotheses
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug I already have a failing test that reproduces a null-pointer crash in the report exporter. Walk me through diagnosing the cause.
evals.expected_output: With a repro in hand, generates 3-5 ranked, falsifiable hypotheses each stating a prediction, grounded in real repo state, before testing any of them.
expectations: Generates 3-5 ranked hypotheses before testing any single one
Each hypothesis is falsifiable — it states a prediction (if X is the cause, changing Y makes the bug disappear/worse)
Ranks hypotheses against real repo state (recent commits, ADRs, quirks/known-issues) rather than blind speculation

evals.name: no-correct-seam-is-a-finding
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug I found and fixed the bug, but the only place a regression test would fit is a shallow unit test that can't replicate the multi-caller chain that actually triggered it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to force a false-confidence test into the wrong seam; instead documents the absence of a correct seam as an architectural finding in Phase 6.
expectations: Does NOT force a regression test into the shallow/incorrect seam that gives false confidence
Records the absence of a correct test seam as the finding — an architectural recommendation filed in Phase 6
Frames the missing seam as the codebase preventing the bug from being locked down, not as an optional nicety

evals.name: no-blind-retry-as-fix
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug the flaky integration test failed, I re-ran it, and it passed. Can we call it fixed and move on?
evals.expected_output: Rejects an intermittent pass as a fix — an unexplained pass means the root cause is still present; it drives toward a higher reproduction rate and a real root cause.
expectations: Does NOT accept 'ran it again and it passed' as a fix
States that an intermittent pass means the root cause is still present
Pushes to raise the reproduction rate (loop the trigger, add stress, narrow timing) to get a debuggable signal rather than declaring done

evals.name: cleanup-gate-removes-tagged-instrumentation
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug I've applied the fix and my debug logs are tagged [DEBUG-a4f2]. What's left before I can call this done?
evals.expected_output: Enforces the Phase 6 cleanup gate: original repro no longer reproduces, regression test passes (or seam-absence is documented), all tagged instrumentation removed via a single grep, and the correct hypothesis recorded in the commit/PR.
expectations: Requires all `[DEBUG-a4f2]` instrumentation be removed from the source under change (verified by grepping that specific tag across the changed source returning nothing) before done
Requires re-running the Phase 1 loop to confirm the original symptom no longer reproduces
Requires the correct hypothesis be recorded in the commit message / PR description for the next debugger

evals.name: offers-built-post-mortem-view
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug is finished: checkout timed out for orders over $1k, the cause was an unbounded retry in the pricing client, and the fix and regression test are in. I would like to click through the hypotheses rather than read the post-mortem.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes the post-mortem as the record first, then offers an interactive post-mortem view built with the checked-in builder from JSON data. It resolves the publish destination from the medium cascade key, redacts secrets before they reach the data, and never writes HTML or script itself.
expectations: Output writes the post-mortem as the record, in the commit message, PR description or notes, before any view is mentioned
Output offers the view in one sentence and builds only after the reader accepts
The view is built by piping JSON to scripts/build-view.mjs, not by writing HTML or script in the session
Log lines and other session text reach the page only as data in that JSON, after secrets are redacted
The publish destination comes from the medium key of the rendered-views cascade, with file as the default when unset

evals.name: belief-checked-before-third-fix
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug the nightly invoice export still drops rows. My loop replays last night's batch and fails every time. Fix one raised the database write timeout, fix two wrapped the insert in a retry; both assumed the database was timing out, and both still fail the loop. What should the third fix be?
evals.expected_output: Names the belief behind both attempts (the database is timing out) in a single sentence, then proposes checking that belief with the replay loop before any third fix. It treats this as advisory: the replay loop stays the gate, and it does not refuse to continue.
expectations: Names the belief behind both attempts (the database is timing out) in one sentence before any third fix is proposed
Proposes checking that belief directly (for example whether any write actually times out) rather than another fix built on it
Does NOT propose a third timeout, retry or similar fix built on the database-timeout belief before that belief is checked
Keeps the replay loop as the pass/fail gate and does not present the belief check as a hard stop

evals.name: uneven-load-gets-tally-script
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug six thumbnail workers share one queue, but workers 2 and 5 hit their memory limit every night while the other four sit mostly idle. I have a loop that replays last night's queue against a local cluster.
evals.expected_output: Writes a small script that tallies jobs or memory per worker and runs it on each replay pass, then compares the passes. If workers 2 and 5 lead in every pass, the next hypothesis is the code that picks a worker for a job. Any fix targets that picking code, not the memory limit or the worker count.
expectations: Produces a script, run on each replay pass, that tallies load (jobs, bytes or memory) per worker, rather than a one-off manual reading
Compares tallies across passes and names the worker-selection code (scheduling, routing or hashing) as the next hypothesis when the same workers lead every pass
Does NOT propose raising the memory limit or adding workers as the fix; any proposed fix changes how a worker is picked for a job

evals.name: failure-after-restart-suspects-stale-state
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug the desktop sync client ran fine all week. Since the machine rebooted this morning it fails on launch with 'unable to open profile'. No code or version changed.
evals.expected_output: Still builds a launch loop first, then ranks stored state above any code hypothesis (serialized state from the previous run, caches, config, lock files) and rules each in or out by renaming it and relaunching.
expectations: Builds or asks for a reproduction loop (launching the client and checking for the error) before testing hypotheses
Lists persistent state (lock files, caches, config or settings files, serialized state) as the first-ranked hypotheses
Proposes a cheap test for each, such as moving the file aside and relaunching
Does NOT start by hypothesizing a code defect when no code changed

evals.name: ruled-out-edits-dropped-before-commit
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug the cause turned out to be a wrong timezone in the report scheduler, and the regression test now passes. Earlier, while testing a connection-pool hypothesis that the logs ruled out, I raised the pool size from 10 to 40 and added a retry wrapper around the query. Can I commit everything now?
evals.expected_output: Edits made for the connection-pool hypothesis, which the logs ruled out, are dropped before the commit: the pool-size change and the retry wrapper come out. The commit carries only the timezone fix and its regression test, and the PR description shows the loop failing before the fix and passing after it.
expectations: Requires reverting the pool size change and removing the retry wrapper before the fix commit
Gives the reason: those edits were made for the connection-pool hypothesis, which the logs ruled out, so they are dropped before the commit
Does NOT approve committing the pool-size change or retry wrapper together with the timezone fix
Asks for the failing loop output from before the fix and the passing output after it in the PR description or report

evals.name: diagnosis-only-stops-at-confirmed-hypothesis
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug just tell me why the CSV importer rejects files that start with a byte-order mark. Do not change the importer; I will write the fix myself.
evals.expected_output: Builds a loop, confirms a hypothesis, and stops there: reports the cause at file:line with the loop output that confirms it, removes any instrumentation it added, and makes no fix and no regression test.
expectations: Builds a reproduction loop and confirms one hypothesis with evidence
Reports the cause with a file:line location and the confirming loop output
Does NOT edit the importer code or write a fix or regression test
Removes any instrumentation it added during the diagnosis

evals.name: check-shaped-prevention-routes-to-owner
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug is done: the report export crashed because a handler called the deprecated datetime.utcnow() the repo bans, and the fix and regression test are in. Write the post-mortem. Both the review and session-flow plugins are installed.
evals.expected_output: The post-mortem answers what would have prevented the bug with a deterministic check for the banned call and routes it to /review:audit-enforceability as a repo or policy mistake, noting the finding goes into a review-findings file first. It proposes the check and does not write a lint rule, hook or analyzer itself.
expectations: Output states that a deterministic check (a lint or analyzer rule, a test, or a hook) would have caught the banned call
Output names /review:audit-enforceability as the owner of that check, not /session-flow:retro, because the mistake is in the repository's code rather than in how the agent worked
Output says the finding is recorded in a review-findings file before that skill runs
Output proposes the check and does not create or edit a lint config, hook or analyzer rule in this run

evals.name: check-shaped-prevention-without-owner-plugins
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug is done: invoice totals were off by a cent because one module rounded with float math the repo bans for money. The regression test sits at the module's public seam and the fix is in. Write the post-mortem. Neither the review nor the session-flow plugin is installed.
evals.expected_output: The post-mortem says a deterministic check for float math on money would have prevented the bug. With neither owner plugin installed and no architectural finding to attach to, it files the check with the issue tracker as its own prevention finding and does not build the check.
expectations: Output states that a deterministic check would have caught the banned float math
Output files the check as its own prevention finding in the issue tracker
Output does not name /review:audit-enforceability or /session-flow:retro as the destination, since neither plugin is installed
Output does not recast the check as an architectural finding, since the bug had a valid test seam
Output proposes the check and does not create or edit a lint config, hook or analyzer rule in this run

evals.name: minimize-red-loop-before-hypotheses
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug my loop is red: replaying one saved POST /orders request returns a 500. The request has 40 body fields, 12 headers and 8 config values set in the test environment. The 500 repeats on every run and matches what the user reported. What next?
evals.expected_output: Before ranking causes, it shrinks the reproduction: cuts one element at a time, re-runs the loop after each cut, and keeps only the elements whose removal turns the loop green. It does not move to hypotheses with the full request.
expectations: Output plans or makes cuts to the request, headers and config one element at a time, with a loop run after each cut
Output keeps an element only when removing it turns the loop green, and drops one whose removal leaves the loop red
Output does not move to Phase 3 hypotheses with the full 40-field request
Output says the minimized case is reused as the regression test

evals.name: forced-red-diff-against-pristine-copy
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug I changed the discount value in the order fixture to -5 to force the test red, and it is red now. Is that red good enough to start the fix?
evals.expected_output: Does not trust the red yet. It diffs the edited fixture against the committed or a saved copy and confirms the edit landed, then checks the test fails for the intended reason.
expectations: Output diffs the edited fixture against the committed version or a copy saved before the edit
Output confirms the edit is present before trusting the red
Output also checks the failure message matches the intended reason
Output does not start the fix before that diff

evals.name: human-driven-loop-keeps-sign-in-out-of-ask
evals.prompt: /debugging:debug the bug shows only after signing in to our staging site, which sends a one-time code to my phone, so no script of yours can reach it. After sign-in, the dashboard shows an empty orders table. Build the loop.
evals.expected_output: Falls back to a human-driven script. Signing in is an instruct step the user does on their own, no ask collects the password, code or other sign-in detail, and the script is handed to the user to run.
expectations: Output drafts signing in to staging as an instruct step for the user
Output has no ask that collects a password, one-time code, token or other sign-in detail
Output asks only for observations, such as whether the table is empty or the copied error text
Output hands the script to the user to run in their own terminal and asks for the results block back
